capabilities: Browse WebDAV and S3 cloud directories in a sidebar
Insert single or batch Markdown links to cloud files
Upload local attachments to the server and rewrite references
Generate signed URLs with sign tokens
Preview images, video, audio, documents and PDFs inline
disambiguation: Not a vault sync tool; it keeps files on the remote server and inserts links to them rather than downloading them into the vault.
extras: README is bilingual (Chinese | English). Notes that object storage may not support iframe preview due to provider restrictions, with a workaround of mounting the storage via OpenList. Office preview is listed as planned. PDF.js is downloaded automatically when selected in Advanced Settings.
motivation: The author describes being a firm believer in the 'Zero-Attachment' workflow in Obsidian and a heavy OpenList user with no coding background, and built the plugin AI-assisted.
problem: Attachments stored in the vault consume local space, and Obsidian has no built-in way to reference files kept on a WebDAV or S3 server.

relations.evidence: Compatible with OpenList, theoretically supports all WebDAV services (Alist, Synology, QNAP, etc.)
the plugin auto-downloads and applies it

summary: Plugin that connects to OpenList/WebDAV and S3 object storage to browse cloud files, insert signed links, and upload attachments out of the vault.
